Create interactive and accessible web forms with validation
Embed images, audio, video and hyperlinks correctly

topics.title: HTML Structure & Anatomy
topics.concept: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) defines the skeleton and semantic meaning of every webpage.
topics.explanation: An HTML document begins with <!DOCTYPE html> followed by <html>, <head> for metadata, and <body> where visible content lives.
keyPoints: HTML is NOT a programming language, but a declarative markup language

Tags usually come in opening and closing pairs:

...

Void elements like ,
, do not have closing tags

topics.title: Headings, Paragraphs & Text Elements
topics.concept: Text hierarchy helps users and search engines navigate content naturally.
topics.explanation:
Use

through

to establish document outline. Use

for paragraphs, for important text, and for emphasis.
keyPoints: Have only ONE <h1> per page for optimal SEO and accessibility
Do not skip heading levels (e.g. going from h1 directly to h4)
Use <span> for inline styling hooks

topics.title: Hyperlinks & Navigation
topics.concept: Links connect pages and resources across the world wide web.
topics.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag with the href attribute allows navigation to other URLs, internal bookmarks, or mailto links.
keyPoints: href attribute defines target URL
target="_blank" opens link in new tab (always pair with rel="noopener noreferrer")
href="#section-id" navigates to an element with matching ID on the same page

topics.title: HTML Forms & Inputs
topics.concept: Forms capture user inputs like credentials, feedback, and search queries.
topics.explanation: A <form> contains elements like <input>, <textarea>, <select>, and <button>. Use the label element to associate textual prompts with inputs.
keyPoints: Always pair <label for="email"> with <input id="email">
Use specific input types: email, number, date, password for automatic mobile keyboard optimization
Use "required" attribute for browser-level validation

topics.title: Semantic HTML5 Architecture
topics.concept: Semantic elements convey meaning to browsers, assistive screen readers, and search engine crawlers.
topics.explanation: Instead of generic <div> tags everywhere, semantic HTML uses specialized tags like <header>, <nav>, <article>, <aside>, and <footer>.
keyPoints: <article> is for self-contained independent content
<section> groups related thematic content together
<aside> represents tangential content like sidebars or author bios

mcqs.question: Which HTML tag is used to define a hyperlink?
mcqs.explanation: The <a> (anchor) tag with the "href" attribute creates hyperlinks to other pages or files.

mcqs.question: Which HTML5 element represents self-contained, independently distributable content like a blog post or news item?
mcqs.explanation: <article> is specifically intended for standalone, syndicated, or independently redistributable content.

mcqs.question: What is the correct input type for entering passwords so characters are masked?
mcqs.explanation: <input type="password"> automatically masks entered characters on screen.

mcqs.question: Which attribute should always be provided on an tag for accessibility and screen readers?
mcqs.explanation: The "alt" attribute provides alternative text for screen readers and displays when the image fails to load.

mcqs.question: How do you open a hyperlink in a new browser tab safely?
mcqs.explanation: target="_blank" opens in a new tab, and rel="noopener noreferrer" prevents tabnabbing security risks.

mcqs.question: Which tag is used to create an unordered bulleted list?
mcqs.explanation: <ul> defines an unordered (bulleted) list, whereas <ol> defines an ordered (numbered) list.

mcqs.question: Which attribute pairs a <label> element with an <input> element?
mcqs.explanation: The "for" attribute on <label> must match the "id" attribute on the target input element.

mcqs.question: What does the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration do?
options: Tells the browser to render using modern HTML5 standards mode
mcqs.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> informs web browsers that the document is written in modern HTML5.

mcqs.question: Which tag is used to define tabular data rows in an HTML table?
mcqs.explanation: <tr> defines table rows; <td> defines table cells (data), and <th> defines header cells.

mcqs.question: Which semantic element contains introductory content or navigational links for a page or section?
mcqs.explanation: <header> represents a container for introductory content or navigation links.

levels.title: CSS Styling, Flexbox & Responsive Layouts
levels.description: Master CSS selectors, box model, Flexbox layout, Grid systems, and mobile-first responsive media queries.
learningObjectives: Master Box Model (margin, border, padding, content)
Build 1-dimensional layouts using CSS Flexbox
Build 2-dimensional grid layouts using CSS Grid

topics.title: The CSS Box Model
topics.concept: Every HTML element is rendered as a rectangular box comprising margin, border, padding, and content.
topics.explanation: Using box-sizing: border-box ensures padding and borders do not unexpectedly expand the element width.
keyPoints: Content: text/images inside the element
Padding: space between content and border
Margin: transparent space outside the border separating neighboring elements
Always use *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

topics.title: Modern Flexbox Layouts
topics.concept: Flexbox distributes space and aligns items along a single axis (row or column).
topics.explanation: Set display: flex on a parent container to turn its children into flex items with powerful justification and alignment options.
keyPoints: justify-content aligns along the main axis (center, space-between, space-around)
align-items aligns along the cross axis (center, flex-start, stretch)
flex-wrap: wrap allows items to wrap onto multiple lines on mobile screens

mcqs.question: Which CSS property ensures that padding and borders are included within the specified element width and height?
mcqs.explanation: box-sizing: border-box tells the browser to account for any border and padding in the values you specify for an element's width and height.

mcqs.question: In Flexbox, which property aligns items along the primary main axis?
mcqs.explanation: justify-content aligns flex items along the main axis (default horizontal row).

mcqs.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root html element font-size?
mcqs.explanation: rem stands for "root em" and is always relative to the font-size of the <html> element.

levels.title: JavaScript Fundamentals & DOM Manipulation
levels.description: Learn modern ES6+ JavaScript, variables (let/const), functions, array methods, DOM events, and async promises.
learningObjectives: Understand variables, primitives, and object references

Handle browser DOM events and state changes

topics.title: Variables, Types & Scope
topics.concept: JavaScript is a dynamically typed language powering interactive web logic.
topics.explanation: Use const for values that are not reassigned and let for mutable variables. Avoid var due to hoisting confusion.
keyPoints: Primitives: string, number, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint
const prevents variable reassignment, but object properties can still be mutated
Use template literals `${var}` for clean string formatting

topics.title: Array Methods (.map, .filter, .reduce)
topics.concept: Functional array methods transform and summarize lists without mutating the original data.
topics.explanation: .map creates a new array by applying a function; .filter creates a subset passing a test condition; .reduce accumulates items into a single result.
keyPoints: Always return a value inside the .map callback
.filter expects a boolean return
Chaining array methods produces clean declarative pipelines

mcqs.question: Which method returns a new array with all elements that pass the test implemented by the provided function?
mcqs.explanation: Array.prototype.filter() returns a new array containing all elements for which the callback returns true.

mcqs.question: What is the value of typeof null in JavaScript?
mcqs.explanation: typeof null returns "object", which is a famous historical bug in JavaScript that was retained for backward compatibility.

topics.title: Git Repositories, Staging & Commits
topics.concept: Git records changes to files over time so you can recall specific versions later.
topics.explanation: Files move from Working Directory -> Staging Area (git add) -> Local Repository (git commit).
keyPoints: git init creates a new local repository
git add . stages changed files
git commit -m "descriptive message" records snapshot
topics.miniExample:
git checkout -b feature/login
git add .
git commit -m "feat: add user login modal"
git push origin feature/login

mcqs.question: Which git command creates and immediately switches to a new branch?
mcqs.explanation: git checkout -b <name> (or modern git switch -c <name>) creates and switches to the branch.

topics.title: State & Component Lifecycle with Hooks
topics.concept: React components re-render automatically whenever their internal state or incoming props change.
topics.explanation: useState declares a state variable and setter. useEffect synchronizes your component with an external system or API.
keyPoints: State updates are asynchronous and trigger re-renders
Pass dependencies array to useEffect to avoid infinite loops
Lift state up when multiple components need to share data

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of the dependency array in the useEffect hook?
options: To control when the effect function executes based on changed values
mcqs.explanation: React compares the values in the dependency array between renders and only executes the effect if any value changed.

topics.title: The Node.js Event Loop
topics.concept: Node.js uses single-threaded non-blocking I/O to handle high concurrency with low overhead.
topics.explanation: Heavy I/O operations are offloaded to Libuv worker threads while the main thread coordinates events.
keyPoints: Single-threaded JavaScript execution
Event-driven architecture
Ideal for I/O-heavy applications like chat and streaming

mcqs.question: Which engine does Node.js use to execute JavaScript code outside the browser?

topics.title: Express Middleware Pattern
topics.concept: Middleware functions have access to req, res, and the next() callback in the request-response cycle.
topics.explanation: Middleware can run code, modify request and response objects, end the cycle, or call next() to pass control.
keyPoints: Order of middleware declaration matters
Error middleware accepts 4 parameters (err, req, res, next)

mcqs.question: How do you pass control to the next middleware function in Express?
mcqs.explanation: Invoking next() passes execution to the next matched middleware function in the stack.

topics.title: Data Modeling & Relationships
topics.concept: Proper schemas prevent data anomalies, enforce integrity, and optimize query latency.
topics.explanation: Choose between embedding documents (1-to-few) or referencing IDs (1-to-many / many-to-many) based on access patterns.
keyPoints: Use foreign keys or ObjectIds for relationships
Index frequently queried fields like email and status
topics.miniExample: SELECT u.name, s.skill_name FROM users u JOIN user_skills s ON u.id = s.user_id;

mcqs.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter records resulting from a GROUP BY operation?
mcqs.explanation: HAVING filters aggregated groups created by GROUP BY, whereas WHERE filters individual rows before grouping.

topics.title: JWT Authentication Architecture
topics.concept: JSON Web Tokens provide a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims securely between client and server.
topics.explanation: A JWT consists of Header.Payload.Signature. The server signs the token using a secret key and verifies subsequent requests without database session lookups.
keyPoints: Never store passwords in plain text—always use bcrypt
Include user ID and role in token payload
Send token in Authorization: Bearer <token> header
topics.miniExample: const token = jwt.sign({ id: user.id, role: user.role }, process.env.JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: "7d" });

mcqs.question: What are the three components of a JSON Web Token separated by dots?
mcqs.explanation: A JWT consists of three base64url-encoded parts: Header, Payload, and Signature.
